narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story and introduces each speech.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God, answering Job out of the whirlwind and judging the friends.

job.name: Job
job.note: The just man of Hus, afflicted and now humbled before the Lord.

1.t: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats bring forth among the rocks, or hast thou observed the hinds when they fawn?

2.t: Hast thou numbered the months of their conceiving, or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

3.t: They bow themselves to bring forth young, and they cast them, and send forth roarings.

4.t: Their young are weaned and go to feed: they go forth, and return not to them.

5.t: Who hath sent out the wild ass free, and who hath loosed his bonds?

6.t: To whom I have given a house in the wilderness, and his dwellings in the barren land.

7.t: He scorneth the multitude of the city, he heareth not the cry of the driver.

8.t: He looketh round about the mountains of his pasture, and seeketh for every green thing.

9.t: Shall the rhinoceros be willing to serve thee, or will he stay at thy crib?

10.t: Canst thou bind the rhinoceros with thy thong to plough, or will he break the clods of the valleys after thee?

11.t: Wilt thou have confidence in his great strength, and leave thy labours to him?

12.t: Wilt thou trust him that he will render thee the seed, and gather it into thy barnfloor?

13.t: The wing of the ostrich is like the wings of the heron, and of the hawk.

14.t: When she leaveth her eggs on the earth, thou perhaps wilt warm them in the dust.

15.t: She forgetteth that the foot may tread upon them, or that the beasts of the field may break them.

16.t: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers, she hath laboured in vain, no fear constraining her.

17.t: For God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he given her understanding.

18.t: When time shall be, she setteth up her wings on high: she scorneth the horse and his rider.

19.t: Wilt thou give strength to the horse or clothe his neck with neighing?

20.t: Wilt thou lift him up like the locusts? the glory of his nostrils is terror.

21.t: He breaketh up the earth with his hoof, he pranceth boldly, he goeth forward to meet armed men.

22.t: He despiseth fear, he turneth not his back to the sword.

23.t: Above him shall the quiver rattle, the spear and shield shall glitter.

24.t: Chasing and raging he swalloweth the ground, neither doth he make account when the noise of the trumpet soundeth.

25.t: When he heareth the trumpet he saith: Ha, ha: he smelleth the battle afar off, the encouraging of the captains, and the shouting of the army.

26.t: Doth the hawk wax feathered by thy wisdom, spreading her wings to the south?

27.t: Will the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest in high places?

28.t: She abideth among the rocks, and dwelleth among cragged flints, and stony hills, where there is no access.

29.t: From thence she looketh for the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.

30.t: Her young ones shall suck up blood: and wheresoever the carcass shall be, she is immediately there.

31.t: And the Lord went on, and said to Job:

32.t: Shall he that contendeth with God be so easily silenced? surely he that reproveth God, ought to answer him.

33.t: Then Job answered the Lord, and said:

34.t: What can I answer, who hath spoken inconsiderately? I will lay my hand upon my mouth.

35.t: One thing I have spoken, which I wish I had not said: and another, to which I will add no more.
